title: Chapter 60 — Multi-Unit Quoting
intro: Quoting multi-unit projects — condos, townhomes, rental buildings, and developments.

sections.title: Multi-Unit Economics
sections.content:
A 50-unit condo project at $3,000 per unit in appliances is a $150,000 order. The margin per unit is lower than retail, but the volume makes it one of the most profitable orders you will write all year.

The key to multi-unit quoting is standardization. The developer wants one fridge, one range, one dishwasher, and one laundry pair across all 50 units. This simplifies installation, warranty, and replacement. Your job is to recommend the right standard package at the right price point for their market.

Ask: 'What are you selling or renting the units for? Who is the target buyer or renter?' A $400K condo needs a different appliance tier than a $1.2M luxury unit. Match the appliance quality to the unit positioning.

sections.title: The Multi-Unit Quote
sections.content:
Present at two or three price tiers. Show the per-unit cost and the total project cost. Include delivery staging — multi-unit projects need phased delivery as units are completed, not 50 fridges on day one.

Include bulk pricing that reflects the volume. Show the savings versus retail pricing. Include installation coordination — who is connecting the appliances? Your team or their electrician and plumber?

The quote should be a complete logistics plan, not just a price list. The developer who sees that you have thought through the delivery phasing, the warranty registration process, and the replacement procedure for DOAs will choose you over the competitor who just sent a spreadsheet of model numbers.

sections.title: Winning the Repeat
sections.content:
Multi-unit developers build more than one project. The developer doing 50 units this year might do 100 next year. Win the first project flawlessly — on time, on budget, zero delivery issues — and the second project is yours without a competitive bid.

Create a post-project summary: units delivered, delivery accuracy, warranty claims, total cost versus quote. Present it at the project wrap-up meeting. 'Here is how we performed. Zero delivery issues, all 50 units on time. Ready to talk about your next project?'
